title: TCS Says US Green Card Suspension Won't Disrupt Workforce Strategy or Hiring
excerpt: TCS says its PERM filings were in the single digits over the past two years, while Washington freezes green card labor certifications for eight major IT employers, including Infosys, Wipro, HCL, and Cognizant.
body:
• Tata Consultancy Services says the US suspension of the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program will have no material impact on its workforce strategy or client engagements, noting its PERM applications were in single digits over the past two years.
  • The suspension, announced Thursday by Vice President JD Vance alongside Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling, halts all new and pending PERM filings involving eight firms: Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL Technologies, and Capgemini.
  • The administration accuses the firms of fraud and abuse of the PERM program, citing federal investigations and excessive H-1B and PERM usage since 2009; no end date has been given for the suspension.
  • What this means for you: if you are an H-1B holder at any of the eight firms, no new PERM certifications will be accepted and pending ones will not be processed — your employer's green card route is frozen for now, though your H-1B status itself is not suspended. Discuss alternatives such as EB-1A or EB-2 National Interest Waiver self-petitions with immigration counsel.

Tata Consultancy Services has moved to reassure employees and investors that the Trump administration's suspension of its access to the US green card labor-certification program will not derail its American operations. The company said its US workforce strategy remains anchored in local hiring and that it plans to keep adding thousands of workers, even as Washington freezes green card filings for eight major IT employers, including TCS itself.

TCS: "no material impact"

In a statement issued Thursday after the suspension was announced, TCS said the US Department of Labor's decision would not affect its workforce strategy or customer engagements. "Our workforce strategy in the US is anchored in hiring local talent," the company said, adding that its PERM applications were "in single digits" over the last two years, "hence this will not impact our workforce strategy."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=1M8q1fXrViI

"Our workforce strategy in the US is anchored in hiring local talent. Our PERM applications were in single digits in the last two years — hence this will not impact our workforce strategy."

— Tata Consultancy Services, company statement

The company's statement to Indian stock exchanges says it intends to hire an additional 15,000 people in the US over the next five years, underscoring the local-first posture it argues insulates it from the freeze.

What the White House ordered

The suspension was announced at the White House on Thursday by Vice President JD Vance alongside Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling, as part of the administration's fraud task force actions against employment-based immigration programs. The named firms — Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL Technologies, and Capgemini — can no longer file new Permanent Labor Certification applications, and the Department of Labor will not process pending ones involving those companies, according to Reuters.

PERM is the mandatory first step for most employer-sponsored green cards. An employer must obtain federal certification that no qualified, willing, and available American worker exists for a specific job before the process can advance. Without it, the bridge from temporary work status to permanent residency collapses.

The administration says the companies abused that process. Vance said, without citing specific evidence, that companies are using the PERM program to replace American employees with foreign workers and undercut wages. "Our message to Microsoft is: You're a great American company, but you've got to hire great American workers," Vance said on Thursday, according to Reuters. Sonderling has pointed to federal investigations and what the administration describes as excessive H-1B and PERM usage by the named firms since 2009.

What this means for Indian tech workers

The freeze lands hardest on the Indian engineers and technologists who form the backbone of these firms' US operations. Many arrived on H-1B visas and spent years in green card backlogs — the wait for Indian nationals stretches well over a decade. With PERM filings blocked, the employer-sponsored path to permanent residency is shut for workers at the eight firms, leaving them tied to temporary status for longer.

The suspension of PERM filings does not, by itself, suspend H-1B petitions — the two programs are legally distinct, and PERM certification is associated with permanent employment rather than temporary work authorization.

The broader crackdown

The PERM freeze is the latest in a series of aggressive moves against employment-based immigration this year. President Trump moved to impose a one-time $100,000 fee on new H-1B visa petitions for highly skilled workers — a measure that has since been blocked by federal court orders, Reuters reported. Other large technology companies, including Meta, Amazon, and Alphabet's Google, remain free to participate in the PERM program — the suspension targets the eight named firms only.

What to watch

Three questions will determine how long the freeze matters: its duration, since the administration has given no end date; litigation, given the H-1B fee was blocked by courts; and the corporate response, as rivals watch whether TCS's local-first posture becomes the industry template.
